en: I'm Salvin Jones, Founder & Director of Entraiot Solutions and the person behind EntraBuild. I grew up in Thanjavur, studied at Maxwell Higher Secondary School, and earned my B.E. in Electronics & Communication Engineering from St. Joseph's College of Engineering, Chennai. I later trained in cloud computing (Linux, AWS, DevOps) at Besant Technologies before founding Entraiot in 2025.

At EntraBuild, I lead strategy, client solutions and hands-on engineering. I've built and shipped a pharma sales-force automation platform for Zivira Labs, a website and ticket-booking platform for Nordic Affairs Media in Sweden, e-commerce sites for silk brands like Bhuvannam Silks and Pavana Silks, a Tamil-first AI biology learning app, and Entraiot Home, our IoT smart-switch dashboard.

My core skills are full-stack web and mobile development (Next.js, Flutter), cloud deployment and DevOps (AWS, Vercel, Render, GitHub Actions), and IoT hardware integration. I enjoy taking a project from first proposal to live deployment.

Outside work, I play cricket, football and chess, and I'm always tinkering with home electronics and wiring projects. What drives me is building technology that solves real, everyday problems for businesses in Tamil Nadu and beyond.

notes.h: From two handwritten books to one screen
notes.s: How we replaced a construction company's delivery-note pad and purchase ledger without changing how they work.
body: R.S.A Construction ran on two books: a delivery-note pad with the same 19 items printed on every page, and a ledger for every material purchase. Both worked, but every total was added by hand, and finding last month's figures meant flipping pages.

We did not ask them to learn a new way of working. The screens copy the books row for row, and the printed delivery note matches the paper pad exactly, so the people who use it every day saw something familiar on the first morning.

Then we added the parts paper can't do: totals that add themselves, stock that updates as materials come in and go out, an Excel export for the accountant, and a WhatsApp button that sends the PDF straight to the customer. Managers get the same tools on their phones.
The lesson we keep: when you replace paper, copy it first and improve it second.

notes.h: Why a pharma company chose to own its sales software
notes.s: Renting software is quick to start. Owning it pays off once your process is your advantage.
body: Zivira Labs had used a rented sales app for years. It worked, but every change they wanted waited on someone else's release plan, and their data sat on someone else's servers.

We started with the daily call report, the screen every medical rep fills in after each doctor visit. After the first demo, their team asked for more detail, and the form grew from 3 fields to 9 within a week. With rented software that request would have gone on a wish list.

Approvals now flow from rep to manager to head office, with a 24-hour window before reports reach admin, and a separate HR portal handles attendance. Zivira owns the code and pays its own hosting directly.
The work is planned in phases, so each phase is paid for only after the one before it is in use.

notes.h: Selling silk sarees without paid ads
notes.s: A small brand, a phone camera and a monthly rhythm can beat an ad budget.
body: Pavana Silks is run by its founder, with no team and no appetite for paid ads after a bad experience. Buyers already came through WhatsApp referrals and Instagram messages, so we built on that.

First, a website worth sharing: a saree that drapes itself frame by frame as you scroll. Then a photo brief anyone can follow with a phone: one flat lay, one draped shot and one close-up of the weave for every saree.
Each month we post, reply and keep the profile active, while the founder handles the sales conversations. Ads can come later, once the organic results show what sells.

faq.q: How much does a website cost?
faq.a: A business website starts from ₹15,000 and usually takes about 15 working days. Online stores and custom platforms are quoted after a short call, because the price depends on what they need to do.

faq.q: How long does a project take?
faq.a: A business website takes about 15 working days. Bigger platforms are built in phases, so you get a first working version early and pay phase by phase.

faq.q: Do you work with clients outside Chennai?
faq.a: Yes. We have an office in Chennai and a branch in Thanjavur, we work with clients in Bangalore, and we have built for clients across India and in Sweden. We work fully in the cloud, so location is never a problem.

faq.q: Do I own the code and the data?
faq.a: On custom projects, the code and the data are yours once the final payment for each phase is made. Hosting can run on your own accounts.

faq.q: Can you look after the website after launch?
faq.a: Yes. Our monthly care plan covers fixes, updates, backups and new features, and we can also handle your social media.

faq.q: Do you build mobile apps and AI chatbots?
faq.a: Yes. We build Android and iOS apps, chat assistants that answer customers and collect leads, and automation that saves your team hours every week.
